art: Cel-shaded anime illustration: flat color fills with exactly one hard shadow tone, crisp black linework of varying weight, expressive posing and a clear silhouette. Energy comes from screentone dot fields and radiating speed lines, never from soft gradients or photographic lighting. Cool paper-white ground, restrained palette with a single vermilion accent. No lettering, speech bubbles, or sound-effect text baked into the image.

background.css: repeating-linear-gradient(115deg, rgba(18,18,26,.03) 0 2px, transparent 2px 26px), radial-gradient(1100px 620px at 50% -15%, #ffffff 0%, rgba(255,255,255,0) 60%), linear-gradient(180deg, #eeeeec 0%, #e0e0dd 100%)

mood: A tankōbon volume open under a desk lamp: cool newsprint paper, true sumi black, and one vermilion ink that behaves like a shout. The theme is loud in its furniture and calm in its prose — but it has to actually be loud, and the one failure it cannot survive is looking like an ordinary web page with a border around it. Signatures to reproduce structurally: (1) PANELS — every card, figure, aside and code block is a panel: 3px solid --ink border, square corners, a hard offset shadow (4px 4px 0 var(--ink), no blur), set tight to its neighbours with a thin paper gutter between them. (2) THE COVER AND CONTENTS GET THE LOUDEST TREATMENT IN THE BOOK, not the quietest — they are the front of a volume and the first thing any reader sees. The cover title is a logo, not a heading: --font-display at 4.5–7rem with line-height .92, set over a screentone field and a speed-line burst, with a --bg knockout box or a 3px --ink text-stroke so it reads on top of the tone rather than inside it. The series/volume line is --bg text knocked out of a solid --ink strip, never grey small caps. The contents is a stack of numbered PANEL ROWS, never a bulleted list: each row is a full-width band separated by a 3px --ink rule, with the chapter numeral set 2.6–3.4rem in --font-display (filled --bg, 2px --ink text-stroke) in a fixed-width left gutter and the chapter title beside it at 1.15–1.4rem in --ink. Give the rows generous vertical padding so the contents fills its leaf instead of huddling at the top of it. A 2.6rem title above a list of .76rem grey numerals is this theme failing. Two layout traps here, both verified by rendering: the hero must be flex:0 0 auto and the logo sized with clamp() — a leaf is a fixed-height box and a flex child shrinks by default, which silently guillotines the title and eats the tagline and byline with no warning. And do not cram the cover hero and the whole contents onto the first leaf: give the hero the top of leaf one and let the contents flow onto the facing leaf. The failure mode to avoid is a small cover squeezed above a small contents list with the facing leaf left almost empty — letting the loud elements take the room they need is what fills the spread. (3) CHAPTER OPENERS carry a speed-line burst behind a huge numeral: repeating-linear-gradient hairlines in --ink at low alpha fanning across the top of the leaf, with the numeral set 9–13rem in --font-display, filled --bg and outlined 3px in --ink via -webkit-text-stroke, so it reads as drawn rather than typed. (4) SCREENTONE, never gradients — any tinted area (asides, table stripes, diagram fills) uses a halftone dot field: background-image: radial-gradient(var(--ink) 1px, transparent 1.2px) with background-size: 6px 6px, at .22–.3 opacity on this light ground. Below about .2 the dots vanish at reading distance and the panel just looks grey. (5) BŌTEN, the manga emphasis dot: `em,.key{font-style:normal;-webkit-text-emphasis:filled dot var(--accent);text-emphasis:filled dot var(--accent);-webkit-text-emphasis-position:over right;text-emphasis-position:over right}` — ship the -webkit- pair, WebKit still wants it. The mark grows the line box, so a marked line sits further from its neighbour than an unmarked one: measured at 17px text it jumps 8px at line-height 1.6 and still 4px at 2.0. Spend bōten on STANDALONE terms — headings, aside titles, table cells, a defined term on its own line — and keep it out of flowing body paragraphs, where the jitter lands mid-column and a fixed-height page has no slack to absorb it; if you do set it inline, give that paragraph line-height 2 or more. (6) SOUND-EFFECT TITLES on asides — heavy display uppercase, a --bg text-stroke with paint-order:stroke fill over a hard --ink shadow, exactly one per aside and never inside the reading column. Pick ONE of two placements and commit to it: fully inside the panel with its own padding, where it may be rotated -2deg; or inset straddling the top border on a --bg knockout, where it must NOT be rotated — a tilted label on a knockout box lets the border cut through the corners of the type, which reads as a rendering bug rather than a design. An inset label needs to be 1.3rem or larger, or it reads as a legend rather than a sound effect. SCALE: this is print, not a web page. Body text sits at 17–18px and any label meant to be read is at least .8rem. A manga leaf carries a few big elements, not many small ones. Body text itself stays plain sumi black on paper — the ink theatrics live in the panels, openers, contents and asides, and the prose column is left completely calm. Keep the spread left-to-right: this is a translated volume, not a flipped one, and the pager depends on it. The feel: a serious technical volume printed by a manga house.
name: Manga
tagline: Sumi ink on newsprint — panel borders, screentone, one vermilion shout
